text: Two weeks of client work here and not one dropped call. The monitor on the desk saved my neck, and the street is silent after 8 pm.
Fast, stable wifi and a proper desk. The chair is a bit hard for full days, so I worked part of the week from the coworking around the corner.
Uploaded several gigabytes of video without any trouble. Some tourist boats in the afternoon, but nothing a headset couldn't handle.
Great light at the desk in the morning. Wifi dipped once during a storm and came back within minutes.
The desk is small, so I took a day pass at the coworking next door for long days. Wifi was reliable for video calls.
Fine for a few days, but working at that tiny desk for a full week was tiring. Construction nearby started at 7 am.
Good value. Calls were clear and the neighbourhood is calm in the evening. Bring a laptop stand.
A real office with a door. My partner and I could both be on calls at the same time without hearing each other.
Excellent wifi and a big desk. A tram passes on the next street, but you only notice it with the windows open.
Productive three weeks. The study gets cold in winter, so ask the host for the extra heater.
Working at the dining table got uncomfortable after a few hours. Weekend nights on the quay were loud until late.
Lovely view and good enough wifi for calls, though screen sharing sometimes lagged. Fine for a week of light work.
Wifi dropped several times a day, and there is no real desk. I ended up working from a cafe most days.
Monitor, good chair and fast wifi: a proper setup. Lunch breaks in the garden were a bonus.
Great desk. The neighbours' kids play in the garden after school, so I scheduled calls for the morning.
Stable connection all month and a coworking five minutes away for days when I wanted company.
Music from the bars below until 2 am, even on weekdays. Wifi could not handle a video call with my camera on.
Cheap and very central. OK for writing and email, but I went to a coworking for every call.
Could not work here. The connection kept dropping and the noise from the street made calls impossible.
You get what you pay for. Quiet enough in the morning to work, lively at night. Bring earplugs.
Our team of three had the study and the kitchen table. Silent house, but the wifi struggled when we were all on calls.
Peaceful and beautiful. Fine for focused writing; large uploads were slow, so plan around that.
Fastest connection I have had on any trip. The monitor desk by the window is perfect for long days.
Ran a full remote workshop from here without a hitch. Some bike bells and canal boats, but quiet indoors.
Great wifi and setup. Saturday nights on the canal get noisy, which mattered less since I don't work weekends.
Expensive, but worth it for a month of deep work. The coworking down the street has good coffee too.
A separate office room with a big desk and fast wifi. Some noise from NDSM events on Fridays.
The office is excellent for calls. The loft echoes a lot, so the living area is less good for a second person on calls.
Reliable wifi all week. Taking the ferry to a coworking in the centre was an easy change of scene.
The attic office is a dream: quiet, bright and away from the rest of the house. Wifi on the top floor is a bit slower.
We worked here as a family of three. One person in the office, one at the kitchen table, both fine for calls.
Twenty floors up you hear nothing. Very fast wifi, and the monitor makes long days easy.
Good desk and a nice work lounge downstairs for a change of scene. The afternoon sun on the screen needs the blinds down.
Wifi was great, but the desk chair is not made for eight-hour days. I bought a cushion.
Calm, green and great for focus. The river view from the desk beats any office I have worked in.
Very quiet and the wifi handled all my calls. The coworking spaces are up in the city, so the lift is your friend.
Perfect silence for writing, but the 4G wifi made video calls choppy. Good for focus work, not for meetings.
Beautiful spot, but I could barely join a call. The desk is a small table in the corner. Better for a holiday than a workation.
A week of deep work with a valley view from the office. Wifi is fine for calls, just avoid huge uploads.
Two of us worked here for a week. The office plus the big dining table gave us both a good spot; the connection slowed in the evening.
